main_body: Rectangular fenced crop plot: a wooden post-and-rail fence around a field of wheat, cabbage and sprout rows, seen mostly from above
top_band: Fence posts: a light brown square cap of about 3 rows (rows 0-3), then a tall front shaft. Rails: a 2-row light top strip (rows ~4-6), then a dark gap, then a second rail. The field is a flat plan with no front face.
evidence: The field, which is the largest volume, is drawn as a top-down plan: crop rows are stacked from above with no south face and no height. The fence posts are flat front-elevation cylinders with a tiny 2-3px cap. The rails are thin horizontal strips with no real top surface, and the side rails are drawn as flat vertical planks. The result is a mix of plan and elevation. No horizontal beam or base shows a foreshortened top over a distinct front face, so it is not a 3/4 frame.

style.evidence: The wood posts have a highlight, light, mid and dark ramp plus grain and knot dots. The crops use 4-5 greens with per-plant highlights. The wheat has dithered speckle in several yellows and ochres, and the soil has grain. Outlines are very dark brown on the wood and dark green on the crops, so they are mostly material-toned but near black in places. Tile density is clearly as high as the reference. The piece has no large flat fills and would sit acceptably next to the Beodeul stall and well.
